About RPM

Roman Pennsylvania Medical, P.C. (RPM) is a telehealth practice dedicated to providing high-quality, patient-centric care. RPM is part of the provider network affiliated with Ro, a direct-to-patient healthcare company. Providers help patients seeking care through Ro’s platform for their mental health, women’s health, men’s health, fertility, metabolic health, and skincare needs.

RPM providers benefit from using technology, tools, and solutions designed to support safe and appropriate care, reduce administrative burden, and help them seamlessly connect with patients throughout their care journeys. As part of RPM’s affiliation with Ro, providers help expand access to affordable, high-quality care to more patients.

RPM’s nationwide network of providers is made up of board-certified physicians, nurse practitioners, and nurses licensed to treat patients in all 50 states and Washington, DC.

As a 6-month contracted Virtual Registered Nurse, you’ll partner with RPM Providers and work independently to provide high-quality patient care through EMR messaging and communications, and triage to ensure safety, productivity, and team optimization are maintained at the practice level.

You are passionate about working in non-traditional healthcare settings and expanding patient access. You can troubleshoot challenging situations as they arise and ensure high-quality patient care is provided per RPM principles and guidelines. You will report to an RN Lead throughout the length of your contract.

Who are you? That's a great question. You are a Virtual Registered Nurse who refuses to settle for the status quo. You apply your nursing knowledge and your desire to help people live happier, more productive lives to your daily work.

You have excellent written and verbal communication skills, you are highly technologically savvy, and you are a problem solver who enjoys working collaboratively with others. We don’t expect you to know everything about medicine or telemedicine, but we do expect you to be ready to dive in and learn.

Provide comprehensive clinical care by independently managing direct patient needs, including message triage, counseling, and education to patients in our sexual health and metabolic health care verticals.
Complete tasks such as side effect management, efficacy counseling, and overall clinical practice support.
Coordinate care effectively by triaging and escalating patient concerns to the appropriate provider groups (Staff RNs, Practitioners, Customer Care, Patient Advocates) according to Ro guidelines.
Triage patient queries and adverse event reports, ensuring they are routed to the patient’s physician, NP, or medical leadership as needed.
Utilize our custom EMR system to answer basic medical questions, educate patients on their conditions and treatments, and offer guidance on lifestyle recommendations and holistic therapies.
Adhere to best practices and company-specific policies for nursing care and treatment.
Review lab results using approved protocols to provide targeted lifestyle coaching and patient education for weight management.
Serve as a resource for the non-clinical Care Team, addressing day-to-day clinical questions and concerns.

The staff nurse working on a Mental Health Residential Rehabilitation Domiciliary is a professional nurse with a broad based clinical knowledge enabling him/her to effectively implement health promotion, prevention and recovery-based programming for adult residents throughout the residential continuum of care.

The Residential staff nurse functions as a part of an interdisciplinary team in partnership with the Mental Health Treatment Team, Veterans, and families promoting wellness through effective holistic, recovery-oriented treatment, and the management of mental health disorders including substance abuse, PTSD, traumatic brain injury, and serious mental illness.

See VA Directive and Handbook 5019.

The Registered Nurse in the Minimum Data Set (MDS) program is responsible for assessing, planning, implementing, coordinating, and evaluating patient care across the continuum of care.

The nurse promotes patient education, self-management, safety, and customer satisfaction while collaborating with the interdisciplinary healthcare team to improve patient outcomes.

As nurses progress from Nurse I to Nurse III, they demonstrate increasing levels of clinical expertise, leadership, independent decision-making, mentoring, quality improvement, and program-level responsibility.

The position requires knowledge of long-term care standards, evidence-based practice, management of acute and chronic illnesses, and palliative and hospice care, while ensuring compliance with Veterans Health Administration, CMS, and Joint Commission requirements.

Key Duties and Responsibilities Assess, plan, implement, coordinate, and evaluate individualized patient care. Administer medications, treatments, and procedures according to established policies and guidelines. Coordinate care, patient education, and self-management activities to support positive health outcomes.

Collaborate with interdisciplinary teams to ensure safe, effective, and patient-centered care. Apply evidence-based practice and participate in quality improvement and performance improvement initiatives. Advocate for patient safety, rights, satisfaction, and ethical nursing practice.

Support professional development through continuing education, mentoring, and knowledge sharing. Lead and contribute to program, unit, or service-level initiatives that improve patient care outcomes and nursing practice. Maintain compliance with VA policies, long-term care regulations, CMS requirements, and Joint Commission standards.

Foster a culture of teamwork, accountability, leadership, and continuous improvement in patient care delivery.

The EBPC is responsible for working collaboratively with the Associate Director of Patient Care and Deputy Associate Director of Patient Care, multidisciplinary teams of clinicians, operational staff, students, and other key stakeholders: Developing, implementing, coordinating, and the evaluation of research related EBP project activities.

Disseminate the results through presentations internal and external to Hines VA, by publicizing best practices through publications, presentations, and other formats to build nursing knowledge. Analyzing nursing practice for gaps in policy or procedure and nursing service practice enhancement opportunities.

Serve as lead for organizing and executing EBP events, including but not limited to the annual EBP training and development. Serve as the EBP subject matter expert (SME) representative to various organizational committees, councils, and as the chair or co-chair of the EBP committee.

Provide oversight of complex health care issues that influence health care and policy development, promoting the VHA vison and mission by adhering to ethical standards for process improvement and scientific inquiry. Participate in the review of literature to assure that policies, procedures, and ethical standards are protected.

Ensure that education programs on the EBP process are in place and effective to meet the needs of nurses. Demonstrate integration of nursing excellence standards resulting in improved outcomes at the team level and beyond.

Collect, analyze, interpret, and report on productivity and other EBP related metrics Support specific EBP, quality improvement initiatives. Develop and implement measures to sustain and grow EBP activities. Develop and test solutions to improve EBP.

Leads both local and organizational level workgroups and committees Ensure that the facility integrates well established EBP models for development, education and processes for improvement. Monitor functional data from EBP and develop interventions to act when necessary. (e.g., staff satisfaction and productivity).

Formulates progress reports as required. Participates in strategic planning and alignment of goals with service level, facility level, and national organization goals. Keep abreast of best practice, research, and relevant clinical information to identify own educational and professional development needs.

The Service Chief of Community Care functions as an advisor, administrator, educator, consultant, and mentor who possesses a wide range of experience and leadership ability.

The Service Chief of Community Care provides senior leadership and oversight for daily clinical and administrative operations within nursing as directed by the Chief of Staff (COS).

The Service Chief of Community Care supports the integration and collaboration of nursing with other professional disciplines and functional areas in the mutual achievement of patient centered and organizational goals.

They champion a High Reliability Organization (HRO) with a culture of safety founded on a systems approach to developing evidence-based health care solutions based on prevention, not punishment, with collective mindfulness.

The Service Chief of Community Care collaborates with interdisciplinary team members, including other program and service leaders at the facility and network. They work closely to establish and maintain effective relationships with all levels of Veterans Affairs (VA) Staff nationwide.

The Service Chief of Community Care relates effectively with customers, families, and the community as well as program and service leaders at the local and network levels. They assist the COS with healthcare operations and the functions and activities expected of them.

The Service Chief of Community Care contributes ideas and recommendations for the establishment of standards of care, policies and objectives for the enhancement of nursing.

The Advanced Practice Nurse (APN) Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner (PMHNP) practices in Mental Health (MH) Service to provide a full range of services emphasizing quality, timeliness, and the advancement of the Veterans Affairs (VA) mission. The PMHNP provides advanced clinical practice, consultation, and management.

The PMHNP practices to the full extent of their education, training, and certification. Core functions are outlined in the clinical privileges that correspond with this position. The PMHNP has prescriptive authority as indicated by their position.

FUNCTIONS OF ASSIGNED DUTIES: The PMHNP is a licensed independent practitioner with advanced education and national certification who provides evidence-based care for a population of patients.

Major duties and responsibilities of the position: Uses advanced clinical judgment to independently provide evidence-based treatment to Veterans with acute or chronic mental illness including use of psychotropic medications, psychotherapy, and other modalities.

Provides patient and family education on medical/MH conditions, preventive measures, and prescribed treatments. Demonstrates leadership and engages in collaboration with other MH and specialty care professionals while involving Veterans and their families (as appropriate), in treatment plan development.

Assesses and adjusts the plan of care as needed to achieve optimal patient outcomes. Counsels and treats patients with substance use disorders. Orders and interprets labs, tests, and diagnostic studies. Initiates referrals and consults to specialty services.

Exemplifies the ICARE core values of-Integrity, Commitment, Advocacy, Respect, and Excellence.

The STAT/Acute Care Registered Nurse provides expert, flexible, and rapid-response care for Veterans experiencing complex or life-threatening conditions.

This RN demonstrates leadership, clinical expertise, and professional accountability by collaborating with interdisciplinary teams, evaluating clinical performance, and contributing to quality improvement initiatives.

The position requires a strong critical-care background and the ability to manage dynamic patient care situations across varied inpatient settings Duties include, but are not limited to: Performs position responsibilities that demonstrate leadership, experience, and creative approaches to management of complex patient care.

Collaborates in the development, implementation, evaluation, and revision of policies, procedures, and/or guidelines.

CTVHCS is in the process of making a cultural change, shifting from a disease-focused approach to a health and wellbeing approach, in order to implement the Whole Health System of Care. This is a VA-wide initiative to provide a comprehensive and systematic approach to improve healthcare delivery at all stages of Veteran care.

This entails moving from an episodic, "siloed" approach to an interdisciplinary, holistic approach, emphasizing self-care in the larger context of well-being.

All staff in this facility will be part of this process, shifting the focus from the question, "What's the matter with you?" to the question, "What matters to you, and how can we help you live your best life?" This strategy also involves integrating a full range of conventional approaches with Complementary and Integrative Health (CIH) approaches in order to optimize lifelong health and well-being, as defined by the Veteran, rather than narrowly focusing on disease management.

A La-Tour-de-Peilz, le Phare-Elim SA, est un établissement médico-social accueillant 46 résidents qui offre un lieu de vie pour des personnes âgées dépendantes et qui dispose aussi d'un Centre d’Accueil Temporaire de 8 places. Nos collaborateurs œuvrent quotidiennement à leur bien-être, tout en favorisant un mode de vie
convivial entre les résidents, leurs proches et les équipes. Pour soutenir l’infirmier chef dans sa mission et compléter l’équipe en place, nous recherchons un.e infirmier.ière diplômée.

· Vous participez à la mise en œuvre des Projets de Soins Individualisés (P.S.I.) et aux projets de vie, en veillant au confort, à la sécurité et au bien-être de nos résidents.
